name: Home Assistant
summary: The state of Home Assistant entities you group by name, such as /ha garage for both garage doors.
description: Reads entity states from Home Assistant's REST API (/api/states/<entity>) on your network, over http:// or, if you turned on SSL, https://, with a long-lived access token. Over https:// it accepts Home Assistant's certificate even if it's self-signed or issued for another name. You choose which entities can be read over the air by putting them in named groups: /ha garage reads every entity in the garage group and replies with each one's name and state, and /ha on its own lists your group names. Nothing outside your groups can be read. Create the token in Home Assistant under your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens.
author: MeshHome

settings.label: Connection
settings.help: Choose https:// if you open Home Assistant at an https:// address (SSL turned on in its configuration or with an add-on).

settings.label: Home Assistant address
settings.help: The IP address or hostname of Home Assistant on your network, with its port (usually 8123).

settings.label: Long-lived access token
settings.help: In Home Assistant, open your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token.

settings.label: Entity groups
settings.help: One group per line: a name, a colon, then up to 6 entity IDs separated by commas. /ha <name> reads that group. Anyone who can use the bot sees the group names, so name them with that in mind.

reply.empty: Home Assistant has no state for that group.
reply.unavailable: Home Assistant isn't answering right now.
